setting_and_country.value: Graduate (master's) psychology programme; country NR in the text
setting_and_country.quote: This quasi-experimental study involved 20 graduate students of psychology—sixteen female and four male.

design.value: Quasi-experimental one-group pretest-posttest with double pretest and a delayed posttest
design.quote: This study was a quasi-experimental study with a one-group pretest-posttest design using double pretests.

participants.value: 20 master's thesis students in psychology (16 female, 4 male; mean age 27.5)
participants.quote: The students were working on their thesis in the third (n = 10), fourth (n = 8), or fifth (n = 2) semester.

group_format.value: GROWTH: one training session (SMART goals, BASE habits) plus four facilitated small-group sessions twice a week over 15 days (16.5 h in total), with daily reflective journals
group_format.quote: The GROWTH program consisted of one training session followed by four sessions of writing groups. The writing groups session were conducted twice a week.

comparison.value: none (the interval between the two pretests serves as a control period)
comparison.quote: the condition between Pretest 1 and Pretest 2 could be regarded as a control condition

other_writing_outcomes.value: Thesis procrastination fell from 72.3 (pretest 2) to 67.3 after the programme and 62.0 two weeks later; F(2.065, 39.226) = 7.854, p = 0.001
other_writing_outcomes.quote: there was a significant effect of writing group program on procrastination F(2.065, 39.226) = 7.854, p = 0.001

notes: Confidence was not measured; the authors cite earlier work that writing groups improve confidence. Small single-group sample; the authors call for a control group.
